title: Negating the RIGHT factor is a separate theorem from negating the left one, in a ring without commutative multiplication
statement: Let R be an AlgS.OrderedRing and a, b elements of R. Then a*(-b) is equivalent to -(a*b). ADR-1616 proved only the LEFT-handed form, (-a)*b ~ -(a*b), and without mulComm -- which AlgS.OrderedRing deliberately does not carry -- the right-handed form does not follow from it: the two are different statements, which the accompanying test asserts by requiring the kernel to refuse to identify their types. The proof goes through AlgS.mul_neg_one on the ring projection rather than through a second additive-cancellation argument: a*(-b) ~ a*(b*(-1)) ~ (a*b)*(-1) ~ -(a*b), of which the middle step is just associativity.

formal.statement: theorem AlgS.OrderedRing.mul_neg : forall (R : AlgS.OrderedRing) (a b : R.carrier), R.equiv (R.mul a (R.neg b)) (R.neg (R.mul a b))

evidence.supports: The declaration is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with an empty Kernel::axiom_footprint, together with every other declaration of ADR-1631's generic Bernoulli layer. The test asserts Environment::contains FIRST, because an absent name has an empty footprint too, and it pins its own name-list length, so a declaration silently dropped from the layer fails it.
evidence.checker_command: cargo test --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --lib rat_prelude::binomial_s::binomial_s_tests::binomial_s_declarations_are_axiom_free -- --exact 2>&1 | grep -c '^test result: ok. 1 passed'
evidence.notes: grep -c, not grep -q: -q would SIGPIPE the producer under pipefail, and -c exits 1 printing 0 when the line is absent, so a suite that compiled to zero tests and exited 0 is caught rather than counted as a pass. --release is mandatory: the rational prelude SIGABRTs on the default debug thread stack.

evidence.supports: The test infers both theorems' types and requires that the kernel does NOT call them definitionally equal, with a positive control (mul_neg's type is definitionally itself) so a def_eq that had stopped deciding would be visible. Without that assertion the claim 'the spine was missing one of them' would rest on reading two doc comments.

notes: One of two generic ring lemmas ADR-1631 needed and the setoid spine did not have; the other is AlgS.OrderedRing.zero_add. Both are reusable well beyond the Bernoulli computation that forced them.
